states.name: Alabama
states.statute: Ala. Code § 36-20-71, as amended by Act 2023-548
states.note: Act 2023-548 raised the bond from $25,000 to $50,000; the bond must be bought from an Alabama-licensed bond producer and approved by the county probate judge.
states.quote: Notaries public shall give bond with sureties, obtained from an Alabama licensed producer of such bonds, to be approved by the judge of probate of the county of their residence, in the sum of fifty thousand dollars ($50,000)

states.name: Arizona
states.note: Bonds are bought in duplicate; the original goes to the Secretary of State with the application.
states.quote: purchase a four-year $5,000 notary bond

states.name: California
states.note: Online notaries need a second, separate $15,000 bond. The commission is void if the oath and bond are not filed within 30 days.
states.quote: a person has 30 calendar days from the beginning of the term prescribed in the commission to take, subscribe, and file an oath of office and file a $15,000 surety bond with the county clerk's office

states.name: Colorado
states.note: No notary bond is required; some notaries buy one voluntarily.
states.quote: a notary does not have to be bonded in Colorado

states.name: Florida
states.note: The bond is filed with the Department of State through a bonding agency with the oath.
states.quote: give bond, payable to any individual harmed as a result of a breach of duty by the notary public acting in his or her official capacity, in the amount of $7,500

states.name: Illinois
states.note: Remote and electronic notaries need $30,000 in total ($5,000 plus a $25,000 bond).
states.quote: a bond for $5,000 with a company qualified to write surety bonds in this State

states.name: Indiana
states.note: Commissions run eight years; a notary holding an older $5,000 bond keeps it until the commission expires.
states.quote: Your uploaded surety bond must be for a minimum amount of $25,000, have an 8-year term, and list your exact name as the principal.

states.name: Louisiana
states.statute: La. R.S. 35:71, as amended by Act 258 of 2025
states.note: In force since February 1, 2026; an errors and omissions policy can no longer be filed in place of the bond. Louisiana commissions are for life, so the bond is kept in force continuously.
states.quote: New law changes prior law to require that notaries public maintain a bond in the amount of $50,000.

states.name: Michigan
states.note: The state's FAQ says the bond generally costs $50 to $100. Michigan attorneys in good standing are exempt. The bond is written for the 6 to 7 year commission.
states.quote: the bond shall be in the sum of $10,000.00 with good and sufficient surety by a surety licensed to do business in this state

official.quote: The cost of the surety bond will vary, generally between $50 to $100

states.name: Missouri
states.note: An errors and omissions policy does not replace the bond.
states.quote: The $10,000 notary bond shall be executed by a licensed Missouri surety for a term of four years commencing on the commission's issue date and terminating on its expiration date.

states.name: Nevada
states.note: The bond is filed with the county clerk of the county of residence.
states.quote: $10,000 (at a minimum) for a 4- year term

states.name: Oklahoma
states.note: Older Secretary of State forms still show $1,000; the current FAQ, instructions and guide say $10,000. The bond is filed within 60 days of the commission.
states.quote: a surety bond in the amount of $10,000.00 signed by one or more sureties must be filed with the Secretary of State

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.note: Since March 28, 2026. A notary commissioned before that date keeps the $10,000 bond until the commission expires.
states.quote: The bond amount is increased from $10,000 to $25,000.

states.name: Tennessee
states.note: A 2025 state TACIR report notes the $10,000 amount has not increased since 1993 and cites bond prices of $30 to $55.
states.quote: Secure a surety bond. Bonds are available through Tennessee insurance companies/agencies that sell surety bond coverage. Provide proof of the bond to the County Clerk.

official.quote: a $10,000 bond at between $35 and $55 ... $30 to $45

states.name: Texas
states.note: The bond is approved by the Secretary of State and payable to the governor; errors and omissions insurance is separate and optional.
states.quote: A notary public must secure a $10,000 surety bond with a solvent surety company authorized to do business in Texas as a surety.

states.name: Utah
states.note: The state notary site says most notary bonds cost about $50; remote notaries need an additional $5,000 bond.
states.quote: a four-year notarial bond of $5,000 is required

states.name: Washington
states.note: The Department of Licensing does not regulate what the bonding company charges.
states.quote: Every notary public must have a $10,000 surety bond in their name.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.note: The surety must be approved by the Department of Financial Institutions.
states.quote: take the oath and file a $500 bond

states.name: California
states.note: Continuous bond on DMV form OL 25; a cash deposit (OL 25E) can replace it. Wholesale-only dealers selling fewer than 25 vehicles a year can claim an exemption (OL 56).
states.quote: are held and firmly bound to the People of the State of California in the penal sum of FIFTY THOUSAND DOLLARS ($50,000)

states.name: Florida
states.note: Filed on FLHSMV form HSMV 86020 in the exact state wording; a $25,000 letter of credit from a Florida bank can replace it.
states.quote: a good and sufficient surety bond or irrevocable letter of credit, executed by the applicant-dealer as principal, in the sum of $25,000

states.name: Georgia
states.note: Used motor vehicle dealers; a separate bond for each licensed location, expiring September 30 of even-numbered years. Parts dealers need $10,000.
states.quote: $35,000 Surety Bond

states.name: Illinois
states.note: Per location, for new and used dealers; the bond must run at least to December 31 of the license year.
states.quote: original $50,000 Illinois vehicle dealer's bond or certificate of deposit

states.name: New York

variants.label: Used or wholesale dealer, 50 or fewer sales last year
Used or wholesale dealer, more than 50 sales last year

states.note: The amount depends on the dealer type and last year's sales. Dealers of trailers, motorcycles, vehicles over 10,000 lb, ATVs, boats and snowmobiles are exempt.
states.quote: $100,000 – Retail or Wholesale Motor Vehicle Dealer (other than New) that sold more than 50 vehicles during the previous calendar year

states.name: North Carolina
states.note: $25,000 more for each additional established salesroom. Form LT-409 (surety) or LT-408 (cash bond).
states.quote: fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) for one established salesroom

states.name: Texas
states.note: Independent GDN dealers since September 1, 2021. Franchised dealers and trailer-only GDNs are exempt. The bond runs two years with the license.
states.quote: all new and renewal GDN license applications must be submitted with a $50,000 Motor Vehicle Dealer Surety Bond

states.name: Virginia
states.note: Required for the first three consecutive years of operation; a lapse restarts the count. Claims above the bond go to the Motor Vehicle Transaction Recovery Fund.
states.quote: the applicant must file a $50,000 bond with the Board

states.name: Washington
states.note: One bond per business location; miscellaneous dealers need $5,000.
states.quote: a surety bond in the amount of: (a) For motor vehicle dealers, thirty thousand dollars

states.name: Arizona
states.note: Set by license type and estimated annual volume. Residential contractors also pay into the Recovery Fund or post a second $200,000 bond.
states.quote: Residential Specialty Contractors | Less than $375,000 | $4,250; $375,000 or more | $7,500

states.name: California
states.note: Required to issue, reactivate or renew an active license. A separate $25,000 bond of qualifying individual can apply to an RME or RMO, and an LLC also needs a $100,000 worker bond.
states.quote: On January 1, 2023, the contractor license bond, bond of qualifying individual, and disciplinary bond, increased to $25,000 as a result of Senate Bill 607.

states.name: Florida
states.statute: Fla. Stat. ch. 489; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61G4-15
states.note: No general contractor license bond statewide. A $100,000 bond applies to a Financially Responsible Officer, and a bond is one way to meet the financial test when the credit score is under 660. Cities and counties may require local bonds.
states.quote: Bonds must be in the amount of $100,000.

states.name: Nevada
states.note: The Board sets the amount when it approves the license, from the monetary limit and the applicant's finances. Residential contractors taking deposits above the AB 39 threshold also post a $100,000 consumer protection bond.
states.quote: the bond can vary in amount from $1,000 to $500,000 based on the type of license, monetary limit, past, present or future financial responsibility, experience, and character of the applicant

states.name: Oregon
states.note: Amounts since January 1, 2024. A contractor with both residential and commercial endorsements posts two bonds.
states.quote: Residential General Contractor $20,000 $25,000

states.name: Washington
states.note: Raised on July 1, 2024 (from $12,000 and $6,000). Contractors with unpaid final judgments post more under WAC 296-200A-030.
states.quote: a Washington Continuous Contractor Surety Bond in the amount of $30,000 for general contractors and $15,000 for specialty contractors

states.name: California
states.note: Needed when regular proof of ownership is missing and the vehicle is worth $5,000 or more. Market value is the midpoint of a valuation guide or a licensed dealer's written appraisal. Bond on DMV form REG 5057, surety signature notarized; a cash deposit can replace it.
states.quote: the bond must be for an amount equal to the market value of the vehicle/vessel
states.valueBasis: market value from a valuation guide or dealer appraisal

states.name: Texas
states.note: Value comes from the Standard Presumptive Value first, then a NADA guide, then a dealer or insurance adjuster appraisal. You have one year from the notice to buy the bond. No bonded title on a vehicle with a lien under 10 years old without a release.
states.quote: The amount is equal to 1 ½ times the value of the vehicle.
states.valueBasis: Standard Presumptive Value, then NADA guide, then appraisal

states.name: Vermont
states.note: The bonded title becomes a regular title after three years.
states.quote: The value of the bond must be one and one-half times the J. D. Power average trade-in value.
states.valueBasis: J. D. Power average trade-in value

freight-broker.quote: A broker must have a surety bond or trust fund of $75,000 in effect.
freight-broker.note: Filed with FMCSA on form BMC-84 (bond) or BMC-85 (trust fund). The section, as amended, applies from January 16, 2026: FMCSA can suspend a broker whose bond falls below $75,000 after a claim payment.

erisa.statute: ERISA § 412, 29 U.S.C. § 1112; DOL Field Assistance Bulletin 2008-04
erisa.quote: A plan official must be bonded for at least 10% of the amount of funds he or she handles, subject to a minimum bond amount of $1,000 per plan
erisa.note: The maximum required is $500,000 per plan official in most cases, $1,000,000 for plans that hold employer securities. The bond covers fraud and dishonesty by people who handle plan money.

miller-act.quote: requires performance and payment bonds for any construction contract exceeding $150,000
miller-act.quote2: the penal amount of performance bonds must equal— (i) 100 percent of the original contract price
miller-act.note: Above $150,000, the performance bond and the payment bond each equal 100% of the original contract price, plus 100% of any increase. From $35,000 to $150,000 the contracting officer picks two or more payment protections instead.

bid-guarantee.quote: The bid guarantee amount shall be at least 20 percent of the bid price but shall not exceed $3 million.
bid-guarantee.note: Federal rule. State and local owners set their own bid security, often 5% or 10% of the bid: read the invitation for bids.

dmepos.quote: must submit to the CMS contractor a surety bond from an authorized surety of $50,000
dmepos.note: Per practice location, with an elevated amount if CMS requires it after adverse legal actions.
